programs.name: B.Sc. Computer Science and Information Technology
programs.description: Flagship 4-year CS program in Nepal blending computing theory, algorithms, and systems engineering.

programs.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level
programs.description: Gold standard international pre-university STEM qualification recognized worldwide.

programs.name: ACM / IEEE-CS Global Standard Computer Science
programs.university: Association for Computing Machinery & IEEE Computer Society
programs.description: The global benchmark defining the core foundational competencies of software engineers worldwide.

programs.name: College Board Advanced Placement (AP STEM)
programs.description: Rigorous college-level curricula and examinations allowing students to earn university placement.

programs.name: GATE Computer Science & Information Technology
programs.description: High-rigor competitive examination testing foundational computer science and engineering aptitude.

courses.name: Introduction to Information Technology
courses.description: Computer hardware architecture, system software, networking protocols, databases, and digital information systems.
learningOutcomes: Understand computer internal hardware architecture and bus structures.
Comprehend base numbering systems, 2's complement, and logic gate conversions.
Explain operating system fundamentals and memory management models.

courses.name: C Programming
courses.description: Structured procedural programming in C covering data types, control flow, functions, arrays, pointers, dynamic memory allocation, and file I/O.
learningOutcomes: Design structured procedural algorithms in C.
Master pointer arithmetic and heap memory management (malloc, free).
Work with file handling and complex user-defined structures.

syllabusUnits.title: Structures & File I/O
subtopics: File Reading and Writing (fopen, fread, fwrite)

courses.name: Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: Comprehensive study of abstract data types, linear/non-linear structures, asymptotic complexity, and graph/sorting algorithms.
learningOutcomes: Analyze algorithm runtime and space efficiency using asymptotic notations.
Implement stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, and graphs from scratch.
Apply greedy, divide-and-conquer, and dynamic programming algorithms.

courses.name: Database Management Systems
courses.description: Three-schema database architecture, ER modeling, relational algebra, advanced SQL, normalization up to BCNF, and ACID transaction recovery.
learningOutcomes: Model business applications using Entity-Relationship (ER) diagrams.
Write advanced SQL queries, joins, views, and triggers.
Decompose relational schemas into 3NF and BCNF without data loss.

courses.name: Operating Systems
courses.description: Kernel architecture, process synchronization, CPU scheduling, virtual memory paging, page replacement algorithms, and file systems.
learningOutcomes: Understand process control blocks, context switches, and thread models.
Prevent race conditions using mutex locks and counting semaphores.
Analyze virtual memory performance and page replacement strategies.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: State-space heuristic search, adversarial game playing, logical inference, Bayesian reasoning, and artificial neural networks.
learningOutcomes: Formulate engineering problems as state-space graph search.
Implement A* heuristic search and Minimax with Alpha-Beta pruning.
Apply Bayesian probability and backpropagation neural networks.

courses.name: Cambridge A-Level Computer Science (9618)
courses.description: Comprehensive international qualification covering information representation, architecture, software, OOP, databases, and algorithms.
learningOutcomes: Master two's complement and normalized floating-point representation.
Construct and trace recursive and object-oriented algorithms in code.
Synthesize processor fetch-decode-execute pipelining and logic circuits.
prerequisites: IGCSE Computer Science or O-Level equivalent

courses.name: Cambridge A-Level Mathematics (9709)
courses.description: Pure Mathematics (Calculus, Trigonometry, Vectors, Complex Numbers) and Newtonian Mechanics.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate and integrate algebraic, exponential, and trigonometric functions.
Solve first-order differential equations and mechanical trajectory problems.
Apply Newton's laws of motion, momentum conservation, and work-energy.

courses.name: Algorithms, Complexity & Computability
courses.description: ACM/IEEE-CS international standard knowledge area covering advanced algorithmic paradigms, complexity classes (P, NP, NP-Complete), and graph analytics.
learningOutcomes: Apply rigorous mathematical proof techniques (induction, invariants, reductions).
Design polynomial-time approximation and randomized algorithms.
Prove NP-completeness through polynomial-time reductions from 3-SAT.

syllabusUnits.title: Tractable vs Intractable Problems (P vs NP)
Approximation & Randomized Algorithms
subtopics: Monte Carlo vs Las Vegas Algorithms

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence & Modern Machine Learning
courses.description: CS2023 updated core covering foundational machine learning, deep neural network architectures, attention mechanisms, reinforcement learning, and AI ethics.
learningOutcomes: Train and evaluate deep convolutional and recurrent neural networks.
Implement multi-head self-attention mechanisms and transformer blocks.
Formulate sequential decision-making using Q-learning.

courses.name: AP Computer Science A
courses.description: College Board certified curriculum covering object-oriented Java programming, control statements, arrays, ArrayLists, inheritance, and recursion.
learningOutcomes: Author robust object-oriented programs adhering to AP Java subsets.
Manipulate 1D and 2D arrays and dynamic ArrayList collections.
Trace and construct recursive algorithms and object class hierarchies.

courses.name: Theory of Computation & Compiler Design
courses.description: Automata theory, regular and context-free languages, Turing decidability, lexical analysis, LL/LR parsing, and code optimization.
learningOutcomes: Construct minimal DFAs, regular expressions, and context-free grammars.
Design LL(1), SLR(1), and LR(1) parsing tables and detect grammar conflicts.
Generate intermediate three-address code and perform basic block optimizations.

courses.name: Digital Logic
courses.description: Boolean algebra, logic gates, combinational logic design, arithmetic circuits, sequential flip-flops, registers, counters, and finite state machines.
learningOutcomes: Minimize Boolean algebraic expressions using Karnaugh maps and Quine-McCluskey algorithms.
Design combinational multiplexers, decoders, encoders, and adder/subtractor units.
Synthesize synchronous sequential circuits and Mealy/Moore finite state machines.

syllabusUnits.title: Boolean Algebra & Logic Gates
subtopics: Axioms and Theorems of Boolean Algebra

syllabusUnits.title: Combinational Logic Circuits
subtopics: Half & Full Adders, Carry Lookahead Adders

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Propositional and predicate logic, proof methods, sets, relations, functions, recurrence relations, combinatorics, and graph theory.
learningOutcomes: Construct formal mathematical proofs using mathematical induction and contradiction.
Model binary relations, equivalence classes, and partial order relations.
Apply graph theory algorithms to network topologies and planar graph colorings.

syllabusUnits.title: Propositional & Predicate Logic
subtopics: Inference Rules and Mathematical Proof Methods

syllabusUnits.title: Graph Theory & Trees
subtopics: Tree Traversals, Spanning Trees, and Planar Graphs

courses.name: Computer Networks
courses.description: Network architecture, OSI & TCP/IP layered protocols, physical transmission, medium access control, IP routing algorithms, transport layer reliable transmission, and socket programming.
learningOutcomes: Calculate subnet masks, CIDR blocks, and design hierarchical IPv4/IPv6 networks.
Analyze link-state and distance-vector dynamic routing convergence.
Implement reliable data transfer protocols and socket programming in Python/C.

syllabusUnits.title: Introduction to Computer Networks
subtopics: Network Edge vs Core, Packet vs Circuit Switching

syllabusUnits.title: Transport Layer Protocols
subtopics: TCP Sliding Window Flow & Congestion Control (Tahoe, Reno)

syllabusUnits.title: Application Layer & Network Security
subtopics: DNS, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTPS Architectures

courses.name: Software Engineering
courses.description: Software life cycle paradigms, agile methodologies, software requirements engineering, architectural design, object-oriented modeling with UML, verification, validation, and maintenance.
learningOutcomes: Formulate SRS documents adhering to IEEE 830 standards.
Model software systems with UML Class, Sequence, and Activity diagrams.
Design test suites executing boundary value analysis, branch coverage, and integration testing.

syllabusUnits.title: Software Process Models & Agile
subtopics: Agile Philosophy: Scrum, Sprint Planning, Standups

syllabusUnits.title: System Modeling with UML
subtopics: Structural Diagrams: Class, Object, Component, Deployment
Behavioral Diagrams: Sequence, State Machine, Activity

syllabusUnits.title: Software Testing & Quality Assurance
subtopics: White-Box Testing: Cyclomatic Complexity, Path Coverage
Unit, Integration, System, and Acceptance Testing (UAT)

courses.name: Advanced Java Programming & Web Tech
courses.description: Java GUI with Swing/JavaFX, Event Handling, Database connectivity with JDBC, Java Servlets, JSP, JavaBeans, and MVC Web Frameworks.
learningOutcomes: Build enterprise desktop applications utilizing JavaFX and multi-threaded event models.
Execute relational CRUD operations using JDBC prepared statements and transactions.
Develop web applications using Servlets, JSP, and Spring Boot REST APIs.

syllabusUnits.title: GUI Programming with JavaFX/Swing
subtopics: Event Delegation Model and Listener Interfaces
UI Controls, Dialogs, and Canvas Graphics

syllabusUnits.title: Java Servlets & Web Containers
subtopics: Session Tracking: Cookies, HttpSession, URL Rewriting

syllabusUnits.title: JavaServer Pages (JSP) & JSTL
subtopics: Expression Language (EL) and JSTL Core Tags

syllabusUnits.title: Enterprise Spring & REST APIs
subtopics: JSON Serialization with Jackson and ORM Hibernate Mapping

courses.name: Cambridge A-Level Physics (9702)
courses.description: Rigorous Newtonian mechanics, circular motion, gravitational fields, oscillations, thermodynamics, electricity, quantum phenomena, and nuclear physics.
learningOutcomes: Solve complex mechanics problems involving circular motion and gravitational orbits.
Model simple harmonic motion and damped/forced oscillations mathematically.
Explain quantum photon energy, photoelectric effect, de Broglie wavelength, and radioactive decay chains.

syllabusUnits.title: Mechanics, Dynamics & Circular Motion
subtopics: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation & Orbits

syllabusUnits.title: Oscillations & Thermal Physics
subtopics: Ideal Gas Laws and Kinetic Theory
First Law of Thermodynamics & Specific Heat

syllabusUnits.title: Electric & Magnetic Fields
subtopics: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws of Induction, AC Transformers

syllabusUnits.title: Quantum, Nuclear & Medical Physics
subtopics: Radioactive Decay Laws, Mass Defect & Binding Energy

courses.name: Cambridge A-Level Chemistry (9701)
courses.description: Comprehensive physical, inorganic, and organic chemistry encompassing chemical energetics, reaction kinetics, equilibrium, transition elements, and organic synthesis pathways.
learningOutcomes: Calculate enthalpy changes using Hess's Law and Born-Haber cycles.
Deduce reaction orders and rate equations from initial rate and concentration data.
Design multi-step synthetic pathways for aromatic and carbonyl compounds.

syllabusUnits.title: Chemical Equilibria & Electrochemistry
subtopics: Brønsted-Lowry Acids, pH, Kw, Ka, and Buffer Solutions

syllabusUnits.title: Inorganic Chemistry & Transition Metals
subtopics: Group 2 Alkaline Earth Metals and Trends
Transition Element Electronic Configurations and Variable Oxidation States
Complex Ions, Ligand Exchange, and d-Orbital Splitting

syllabusUnits.title: Organic Chemistry & Analytical Spectroscopy
subtopics: Carbonyls, Carboxylic Acids, and Nitrogen Compounds (Amines, Amides)
Infrared Spectroscopy, Mass Spectrometry, and 1H/13C NMR

courses.name: Cybersecurity & Defensive Programming
courses.description: Cryptographic foundations, authentication and access control, network intrusion defense, web security (OWASP Top 10), and secure software design practices.
learningOutcomes: Implement symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic algorithms correctly without known implementation flaws.
Audit source code for buffer overflows, race conditions, and SQL injection vulnerabilities.
Architect zero-trust access control and secure API communication protocols.

syllabusUnits.title: Web Application Security & OWASP Top 10
subtopics: SQL Injection, Command Injection, and Mitigation
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and Content Security Policy (CSP)
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and Deserialization Exploits

syllabusUnits.title: Defensive Systems & Network Security
subtopics: Memory Safety: Buffer Overflows, ROP Gadgets, ASLR, DEP
TLS 1.3 Protocol Mechanics and Certificate Revocation

courses.name: AP Calculus BC
courses.description: Complete university calculus covering differential and integral calculus, differential equations, sequences, infinite series convergence tests, Taylor series, and parametric/polar/vector functions.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate indefinite and improper integrals using integration by parts, partial fractions, and trigonometric substitutions.
Determine convergence or divergence of infinite series using ratio, root, integral, and comparison tests.
Construct Taylor and Maclaurin polynomial series approximations and bound truncation error using Lagrange error bounds.

syllabusUnits.title: Limits, Continuity & Differentiation
subtopics: Product, Quotient, Chain Rules, Implicit Differentiation
Mean Value Theorem and Related Rates

syllabusUnits.title: Integration Techniques & Applications
subtopics: Integration by Parts & Partial Fraction Decomposition
Improper Integrals with Infinite Limits or Discontinuities

syllabusUnits.title: Differential Equations & Slope Fields
subtopics: Logistic Growth Models and Carrying Capacity

syllabusUnits.title: Parametric, Polar & Vector Functions
subtopics: Polar Coordinates, Derivatives, and Enclosed Area Integrals

syllabusUnits.title: Infinite Sequences & Series
subtopics: Convergence Tests: Divergence, Integral, p-Series, Comparison
Ratio and Root Tests, Radius of Convergence
Taylor & Maclaurin Series, Lagrange Error Bound

courses.name: GATE Data Structures & Algorithms
courses.description: Rigorous competitive algorithms, asymptotic time/space complexity analysis, balanced search trees, graph algorithms, divide-and-conquer, greedy heuristics, dynamic programming, and NP-completeness.
learningOutcomes: Prove asymptotic upper and lower bounds using Master Theorem and substitution methods.
Execute tree balancing rotations on AVL and Red-Black trees under insertion/deletion.
Design optimal polynomial-time algorithms using dynamic programming and greedy strategies.

syllabusUnits.title: Asymptotic Analysis & Recurrences
subtopics: Recursion Tree Method and Akra-Bazzi Method

syllabusUnits.title: Linear & Non-Linear Data Structures
subtopics: Arrays, Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues, Circular Queues
Binary Search Trees (BST), AVL Trees, Red-Black Trees
Binary Heaps, Priority Queues, and Disjoint Set Union (DSU)

syllabusUnits.title: Graph Algorithms & Shortest Paths
subtopics: Topological Sort and Strongly Connected Components (Kosaraju, Tarjan)
Minimum Spanning Trees: Kruskal and Prim Algorithms

syllabusUnits.title: Dynamic Programming & Greedy Algorithms
subtopics: Greedy Choice Property: Fractional Knapsack, Huffman Coding
Optimal Substructure: 0/1 Knapsack, Matrix Chain Multiplication
Longest Common Subsequence (LCS), Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS)

syllabusUnits.title: NP-Completeness & Advanced Topics
subtopics: Classes P, NP, NP-Hard, and NP-Complete
Polynomial-Time Reductions (3-SAT to CLIQUE, Vertex Cover)
String Matching: KMP and Rabin-Karp Algorithms
